speaker: Doctor
text: Your highest recorded temperature was 39.2°C, and you report no foul-smelling lochia, which makes endometritis less likely despite the uterine tenderness. Given the dysuria, frequency, and fever, I suspect a urinary tract infection or pyelonephritis rather than a primary uterine issue. Let's wait for the urinalysis and blood count results to confirm the source of the infection.

speaker: Patient
text: Complains of minor difficulty in breathing but denies any urinary pain, headache, vomiting, or diarrhea.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned difficulty breathing, which is a concerning new symptom. Do you have any chest pain or cough, and have you noticed any swelling or pain in your legs? REQUEST TEST: D-Dimer

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal D-dimer effectively rules out pulmonary embolism, so I will focus on the urinary tract. Given the high fever and urinary symptoms, I suspect acute pyelonephritis. REQUEST TEST: Urine_Culture

speaker: Doctor
text: With a normal D-dimer and a normal urine culture, pulmonary embolism and pyelonephritis are effectively ruled out, yet you have a high fever and uterine tenderness. I must reconsider endometritis as the primary cause, so I will request a pelvic ultrasound to check for any retained placental tissue or abscess. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the high fever, uterine tenderness, and leukocytosis in the postpartum period with negative workup for other sources, the clinical picture is most consistent with endometritis, which can present with normal imaging in early stages. DIAGNOSIS READY: Endometritis
